summary: GRAVEYARD structural pass mapped the same provisional 12-company batch to durable needs and likely successor bottlenecks without promoting edges. GEV remains the only company with audited canonical causal structure. Fresh filings sharpen two causal risks: IONQ has vertically integrated toward semiconductor fabrication through SkyWater but inherits foundry/integration/capital constraints; NBIS's $5.0B convertible financing highlights capital availability as a potential successor bottleneck to AI-compute expansion. All other mappings remain hypotheses requiring independent primary constraint evidence.

materialFindings.finding: IONQ's completed SkyWater acquisition moves part of the quantum stack toward domestic semiconductor fabrication/packaging, potentially reducing foundry dependence while creating integration, capital and manufacturing-execution successor constraints.

NBIS's upsized $5.0B convertible financing is direct evidence that capital availability is material to scaling its AI infrastructure; whether capital is the binding successor bottleneck versus power, GPUs, networking or customer demand remains unresolved.

GEV retains audited company-linked causal edges and independently established grid/transformer/interconnection successor constraints from prior Chief-reviewed work; no new canonical edge is proposed this pass.

accuracyDebates.topic: Does a large financing prove capital is the binding bottleneck?
accuracyDebates.position: No. It proves capital is material, not uniquely binding; power, compute hardware, interconnect and demand must be tested as alternatives.
